claims.claim: Epiphanius of Salamis was bishop of Salamis, Cyprus, and lived approximately 315–403 AD.
Epiphanius was born near Eleutheropolis in Palestine.
Epiphanius was consecrated as Bishop of Salamis in 367.
Epiphanius served as bishop for nearly forty years until his death in 403.
The work De prophetarum vita et obitu is attributed to Epiphanius in manuscripts, though the attribution is disputed as it also appears under other names such as Dorotheus and anonymous authors.

The work survives in multiple recensions, including at least two attributed to Epiphanius, one attributed to Dorotheus, one anonymous version, and a recension with scholia by Hesychius and other fathers.
The work treats the lives and deaths of prophets, giving details of their tribal origins, birthplaces, and places of burial.
A critical edition of the work was published by Theodor Schermann in 1907 under the title Prophetarum vitae fabulosae.
The work is catalogued as CPG 3777-3778 in the Clavis Patrum Graecorum.
Epiphanius was known for his strong defense of orthodoxy and his opposition to Origenism.
Epiphanius's best-known work is the Panarion, a compendium of eighty heresies.
